title: About
body:
Since the 1990s, there has been a proliferation of international efforts to confront the “difficult past” between countries. A key feature is the cross-national dialogue among historians from countries involved in past conflicts. Over twenty bilateral Joint Historians’ Commissions (Ger. *Gemeisamen Historiker Kommission*) have been set up in Europe and elsewhere. These history commissions raise important questions about the role of historians and historical knowledge in post-conflict resolution and reconciliation between nation-states. They also pose challenging questions about historical knowledge at a time when universal truth in history is no longer self-evident.

This digital archive aims at bringing together information about joint historians’ commissions or other similar endeavors from across the world. Through a comparative study of these cross-national dialogues, it is hoped that one gains a better understanding of the production of historical knowledge and their role in international conflict resolution today.
